event.title: Halloween Nonstop: DJ Stingray, Convextion, Rene Wise, Juliana Huxtable, DJ Koolt + more
event.content:
Mischievous spirits descend as the planets align to bring you a Halloween Nonstop that goes full-tilt freak mode all weekend long.

The veil is lifted on Friday when local staple COTTON leads us down wormholes of electro-tech witchcraft, followed by shapeshifting rhythmic sorcery from XOXA’s Tammy Lakkis and a hypnotic live set of otherworldly electronics from veteran psychonaut Convextion.

On Saturday morning, IMOGEN conjures the sun with hard acid and electro, and the one and only masked Detroit legend DJ Stingray keeps the cauldron piping hot and fast-bubbling. Incomparable sonic sorceress Juliana Huxtable’s ever-shifting invocations carry us into the afternoon, followed by a whirlpool of ethereal, driving delights from Sweden’s Philippa Pacho.

Darkness falls once again as London's Rene Wise dishes up rolling, kaleidoscopic techno, followed by webs of pumping, sticky grooves from local hypnotist LYDO. And the late night hours are enchanted with heady, low-end expertise and pulsating, percussive flair by Berlin’s ābnamā and Nowadays own, DJ G.

On Sunday morning, we enter the home stretch with Brazil's prince of party-rocking and Nowadays resident, RHR, taking over at 6am before DJ Koolt arrives from Uruguay with a sizzling acid techno bath. Vladimir Ivkovic brings things to a close with his signature strain of genre-agnostic, hypnotic psychedelia.

///

Entry is at the discretion of our door staff. Halloween is a time for creativity, irreverence and self-expression, but costumes involving racist caricatures, hateful imagery or degrading stereotypes are not welcome at Nowadays.

Online purchases are limited to four tickets maximum per person. If tickets are sold out here, we always hold a good amount at the door. We will do our best to admit those without tickets but entrance is not guaranteed.

Nonstop tickets are divided by entry time. You must arrive during the hours listed on your ticket. For example, if you buy a "10PM–4AM" ticket, you must get here between 10pm and 4am.

After you've arrived during your designated time window, you can stay as long as you'd like, so long as you abide by our safer space policy (more on that below). You're also welcome to come and go as you please. Re-entry is based on capacity and is not guaranteed.

Nonstop attendees can attend Mister Sunday in the backyard starting at 3 pm without buying a separate ticket, and Nonstop re-entry is honored during Mister Sunday.

Violence, non-consensual touching, racist, homophobic, transphobic, sexist, ageist or other discriminatory language, and leering are not allowed within our walls or in our back yard. If someone says or does something to make you feel uncomfortable while you’re here, let us know.

///

Accessibility:

The wheelchair entrance to our indoor space is in the driveway, which is the access point most commonly used to enter Nowadays. During parties the driveway gate is locked, so please ask staff at the street entrance for assistance with entry.

All of our bathrooms are gender-neutral. There is one accessible stall indoors. Just ask any Nowadays staff member for the key, and they can show you the way. During parties, seating is available both on and off the dance floor. While we don’t have a dedicated quiet space indoors during parties, the booths next to coat check are a little quieter, and the deck and back yard a little quieter than that. Most nighttime parties include the use of strobe lights and water based haze.

event.title: BOUND Blackout: Laure Croft / SKIN / Katie Rex / Kim Anh / Dj Warning / likeholywine / nonsuit
event.content:
FETISH ATTIRE MANDATORY

Laure Croft, the Tune Raider herself, makes her BASEMENT debut for BOUND. The Dutch-born, Berlin-based artist lives by one rule alone: “keep it sexy.” Since 2024, she’s been at the helm of her SEXYRECS label, which has already assembled a remarkable roster. Her vinyl-heavy sets strike an essential balance: scorching techno, coursing, atmospheric grooves, decisive power all come into play. Running on pure selections and honed technique with no excess of flash, Croft oozes the kind of confidence in the booth that makes it impossible not to lock in. Skin also arrives in the room for the first time. This one is special - Skin made her name as the lead singer for the iconic rock-electronic group Skunk Anansie, whose work across the ‘90s blended elements of heavy, confrontational punk and grunge with industrial and electronica. As a solo artist, she has channeled that intensity into her techno sets, bringing the same galvanizing power that has made her such a figurehead. BOUND founder Katie Rex completes the lineup, driving the night home with a dose of pure hardgroove and thundering, noise-caked techno. 

San Francisco’s Squish joins for their second STUDIO takeover. The party series has grown into one of the key hubs of queer nightlife in a city that is already historic for its deep history of LGBT+ art, culture and political activism. Extending that lineage, Squish has invited some of the most thrilling artists from around the globe to the Bay Area for community-forward events whose impact reverberates far beyond their hometown. Kim Anh headlines the night. The STUDIO mainstay has spent years developing her own unique interpretation of dance music. Rooted in the glimmering vistas and charged glamor of the ‘80s, Anh has crafted a body of work that finds timelessness in hyperspecificity. DJ Warning returns from LA following this June’s debut at the club. This May, he released “Fist Pumpers United,” a three track EP that pulls no punches. At the center of the batch sits “Move Your Body,” a track that reworks Marshall Jefferson’s anthemic classic of the same name. Warning’s statement rings through loud and clear. Even as he invokes a pillar of the genre, he makes it own. Squish co-founders likeholywine and Nonsuit complete the lineup with one of their signature b2bs. likeholywine drills right down to the core with heavy, pumping house, no questions asked, while Nonsuit adds a touch of depth and dubby reverberance. 

■ No photos or videos
■ Ticket purchase does not guarantee entrance
■ No phone use on the dancefloor
■ The dance floor is for dancing, not conversation
■ No glowing/flashing clothes or items
■ Respect other people's space, no shuffling
■ Consent is mandatory
■ Zero tolerance for racism, homophobia, transphobia, sexism, ableism or any form of discrimination
■ Take care of each other, alert our staff if somebody isn't feeling well
■ Violating the house rules will result in removal

An email with event details/location will be sent to ticketholders at 9pm on 10/30!

We'll have a robust team working to ensure the vibes and our guests are safe and comfortable. Admittance is at the discretion of our door staff. Tickets do NOT guarantee entry, and removal for violation of any of our policies below do not constitute a refund.

---

Merge is a Brooklyn-based, queer party that aims to cultivate sonic liminoid experiences through techno music. We will work together to incubate the collective queer body, and experience its transformation under the influence of techno. We seek release, mutual understanding, deeper access to the personal, interconnected, and ethereal. We honor the sound through dance, self expression, and hyper-immersion.

---

We have zero tolerance for physical, verbal, or sexual harassment. This includes non-consensual touching, violence, discriminatory language, or any behaviors that have a negative impact on the experience or the physical safety of other guests. If a problem or concern arises, guests are encouraged to locate a staff member for assistance. While on the dance floor, we encourage guests to keep conversations to a minimum and phones in their pockets.

Come correct and ready to sweat!

event.title: WHOREPOCALYPSE w/ Zutzut, 2AT, RICO RICA, DJ Rankng, Sterling Juan Diaz, Litney + more
event.content:
Whorechata's WHOREPOCALYPSE returns bigger than ever, taking over two rooms for the first time and featuring the best from the underground communities reshaping Latin club culture across the U.S., Mexico, Colombia and beyond. 

Expect a cross-border lineup of artists taking it into harder, darker, and sexier territory. Making their Whorechata debut, Zutzut (CDMX) has been a pioneering force blending Latin rhythms with electronic club beats for more than a decade. Joining him will be 2AT (Bogotá), DJ Ranking (CDMX), Rico Rica (Barranquilla) and Iris Estefanía (CDMX). The second room pays homage to the scenes closer to home, with Sterling Juan Diaz (NYC) and Litney (Toronto) joining Whorechata residents Roman Sensation and OYYSTER for a collision of high-energy Latin techno, dembow, bubbling and more.

The WHOREPOCALYPSE is a space that centers queer and trans Latinx, people of color and their allies. Produced in collaboration with LEAK NYC.
